fixes.replace: Clusters 1 and 2 have the closest centers, but both are large, and the factor $pq/(p+q)$ is at most the size of the smaller cluster, and near it when one cluster is much larger.
fixes.why: For the merge of clusters 1 and 2 that opens this sentence, pq/(p+q) = 30*30/60 = 15 against a smaller cluster of 30, exactly half of it, so 'close to' is false for the very case being named; the bound pq/(p+q) <= min(p,q) always holds, and the merges with cluster 3 give 30*6/36 = 5 against a smaller cluster of 6, which is the case where the factor really is near the smaller size.
